messages:
maria_sales: ACME POC — free credits dropped to 0 overnight; customer sees ~12k tokens in console but billing shows ~36k. @sam_se can you triage? :eyes:
sam_se: on it. do we have example request ids / timestamps?
maria_sales: they sent an excerpt via email. quick paste: `billing_event: {customer_id: acme, tokens: 24000, plan: poc_free}`. they also reported repeated 429s for a subset of calls.
kai_eng: 429s usually mean rate-limiter. retries could explain inflated tokens if client retried full prompt each time. do we have the client retry behavior?
maria_sales: customer says client retried ~5x per call. snippet they sent: `HTTP 429: rate_limit_exceeded, retry-after: 1`
sam_se: retries could definitely multiply token accounting. check for duplicate request_id within short windows. try: `curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" "https://console.redwood.ai/usage?customer=acme&since=2026-03-19" | jq .`
kai_eng: i'll grep the runtime logs and billing-ingest. also check webhook dedupe keys — sometimes webhooks refire and billing ingest doesn't dedupe.
maria_sales: also their spend-alerts fired repeatedly then stopped — they want to know why quota didn't block after repeated alerts.
anya_finance: do we bill for failed requests? i thought we exclude 4xx/5xx but need to confirm pipeline semantics.
lucy_support: quick glance: billing-ingest currently writes raw events then marks billed only when `billing_ack=true`. but the summation job sums tokens from raw events as they come in. pulling raw events now.
sam_se: found a cluster of identical request_ids between 2026-03-19T02:12:05Z and 02:12:18Z where client retried. example log:
```
2026-03-19T02:12:05Z request_id=abc123 attempt=1 tokens=512 status=429
2026-03-19T02:12:06Z request_id=abc123 attempt=2 tokens=512 status=429
2026-03-19T02:12:07Z request_id=abc123 attempt=3 tokens=200 status=200 billing_ack=true
```
kai_eng: that matches a billing anti-pattern i've seen — ingest sums tokens on first write, billing_ack applied later but we never subtract the earlier counted tokens. looks like a race where retries create multiple raw events that get summed.
anya_finance: if true, we need to credit acme and fix pipeline asap.
maria_sales: customer expects refund/credit and wants spend-alerts tuned so this doesn't blindside them again. can we ship a hotfix today?
kai_eng: short-term mitigation: change billing-ingest to dedupe by `request_id` and only emit token-count metrics once `status=200` or `billing_ack=true`. i'll roll a canary to the poc-customers-small group.
lucy_support: i'll prepare a runbook to identify affected customers. proposed query: `select distinct customer_id from billing_events where created_at between "2026-03-19" and "2026-03-20" and request_id in (select request_id from billing_events where status=429)`
sam_se: i'll handle comms. once kai confirms credit amount i will send ACME the credit memo draft.
maria_sales: :thumbsup: ping legal if the credit > $5k. also let's add a note to POC onboarding about client retry/backoff guidance and recommended SDK config.
kai_eng: deploying canary now (group: poc-customers-small). i'll monitor token-sum and billing pipeline logs; ETA ~45m.
anya_finance: prepping provisional credit so we can apply immediately if fix validated. need estimated exposure number.
lucy_support: collecting affected request_ids and opening a support ticket with ACME context. tagging @billing_bot to queue credit once we have approval.
billing_bot: billing-bot: queued credit request for customer acme, ref TKT-9876, awaiting human approval.
sam_se: thanks all — i'll update ACME in ~1h or sooner after canary shows clean ingest. maria, can you schedule a short call if they want it?
maria_sales: scheduling now. ty team :heart:
